question.problem:
The data below is taken from the table of values of the cumulative distribution function $Φ(z)$ for the standard normal distribution. Given that $Z∼N(0,1),$ compute $P(Z<2.17).$ Use the table below and do not round your answer.

| $z$ | $\,0.05\,$ | $\,0.06\,$ | $\,0.07\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\,2.0\,$ | $\,0.9798\,$ | $\,0.9803\,$ | $\,0.9808\,$ |
| $\,2.1\,$ | $\,0.9842\,$ | $\,0.9846\,$ | $\,0.9850\,$ |
| $\,2.2\,$ | $\,0.9878\,$ | $\,0.9881\,$ | $\,0.9884\,$ |

$P(Z<2.17)=$
{{field-1}}
question.worked_solution:
If $Z∼N(0,1),$ then by the definition of the cumulative distribution function $Φ(z),$ 

$$
P(Z\le z)=Φ(z).
$$

Also, since $Z$ is continuous, 

$$
P(Z<2.17)=P(Z\le 2.17)=Φ(2.17).
$$

The required probability is represented by the area shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14254773/assets/c1d8ba1ea5e9b0362fa59a5993e4292dde7b4dd8a8694c71f9dbec026fa3e821.png)

Now, we determine the value of $Φ(2.17)$ from the table:

- We first select the row that corresponds to $2.1$ and the column that corresponds to $0.07.$

- Then, we take the value that lies at the intersection:

| $z$ | $\,0.05\,$ | $\,0.06\,$ | $\,0.07\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\,2.0\,$ | $\,0.9798\,$ | $\,0.9803\,$ | $\,0.9808\,$ |
| $\,2.1\,$ | $\,0.9842\,$ | $\,0.9846\,$ | $\,0.9850\,$ |
| $\,2.2\,$ | $\,0.9878\,$ | $\,0.9881\,$ | $\,0.9884\,$ |

Therefore, according to the table, we have

$$
P(Z\le 2.17)=Φ(2.17)=0.9850.
$$
